newsitem.title: CANADA: Drug suspect ordered extradited to U.S. from Canada.
newsitem.headline: Drug suspect ordered extradited to U.S. from Canada.

text.p: A suspected Colombian cocaine dealer on Tuesday was ordered extradited from Canada to face trial in the United States in connection with a $4 million drug deal, according to a report from the Canadian Press news agency.
Justice Jack Waite rejected an argument that Orlando Cordero's alleged crime was committed in Canada.
Cordero, 48, a Colombian who was living in Calgary, was accused of conspiring with others to sell up to 440 pounds (200 kg) of cocaine to an undercover officer.
Royal Canadian Mounted Police Constable Bruce Romaniuk said he and a civilian informant arranged through Cordero to purchase the drugs at a cost of $4 million.
Romaniuk said he was directed by Cordero to a contact in New York City, who was to provide the cocaine.
Justice Waite said his job wasn't to decide if an offence was committed in Canada, but whether there was sufficient evidence to warrant a U.S. trial.
"That evidence has to be looked at through American eyes, not Canadian eyes," he said. "On the basis of (the evidence) a jury, properly instructed and acting reasonably, might convict."
Cordero has up to 30 days to appeal the ruling or seek the intervention of Justice Minister Allan Rock.
